I hadn't seen my college roommate in almost ten years.
We graduated and went our separate ways, and it was one of those friendships that just fades out slowly, without any actual falling out.
I was flying home for a family visit, half asleep in the boarding area.
I was scrolling through my phone, not paying much attention to the people around me waiting for the same flight.
Boarding started, and I shuffled toward the gate with everyone else.
I found my row and looked up to see who I'd be sitting next to for the next few hours.
It took a solid few seconds before it actually clicked.
The face looking back at me, a little older, with a slightly different haircut, definitely belonged to my old roommate, sitting right there in the seat next to mine.
For a moment I genuinely thought I was imagining things.
My tired brain does that sometimes in crowded places, especially when I'm running on very little sleep.
We both just stared at each other for a second.
Then we started talking at the same time, both saying some version of "wait, is that actually you?" loud enough that people nearby glanced over.
The flight attendant had to ask us twice to quiet down during the safety demonstration.
We were too busy catching up on a decade of missed birthdays, jobs, moves, and mutual friends we'd both lost touch with.
The guy sitting on my other side eventually just gave up trying to nap and joined the conversation a little.
He laughed along at some of the more ridiculous college stories we kept dragging back up from a decade ago.
Turns out, she now lived one city over from me.
Neither of us had any idea about that, despite apparently living less than an hour apart for the past two years without ever crossing paths.
We spent a solid ten minutes just listing off places we'd both probably been to at the same time.
The same grocery store.
The same gym.
Even the same coffee shop, on a couple of occasions.
We exchanged numbers again, properly this time, and actually followed through.
We grabbed coffee a couple weeks later, back on solid ground, laughing again about how ridiculous the whole airplane reunion had been.
We've kept in touch properly ever since.
We grab dinner every few weeks now, and honestly, it feels like we picked up almost exactly where we left off a decade ago, just with slightly better jobs.
I still think about the odds sometimes, that out of an entire airport full of people, we ended up in seats right next to each other.
